title: How to use a needle minder for cross-stitch
subtitle: Keeping your needle secure on the fabric between stitching sessions
excerpt: A needle minder is a pair of magnets used to hold a cross-stitch needle on the surface of the fabric when it is not in use. One magnet sits on the front of the Aida; a second, stronger magnet sits on the back and holds the front magnet in place through the fabric. The needle is held between the front magnet and the fabric surface.
sourceNotes: Needle minder use for cross-stitch. Standard craft accessory guidance.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.

content.text: A needle minder solves the problem of where to park the needle when you need both hands free or when you set the project down. Rather than jabbing the needle into the
and risking a hole in the fabric, or dropping the needle and losing it, the needle minder holds it safely on the fabric surface.
Separate the two magnets. The smaller, decorative magnet is the front piece; the larger, stronger magnet is the back piece.
Place the back magnet behind the Aida in the margin area where there is no stitching. The back magnet should be in the unstitched border, not under the design area.

Place the front magnet on the face of the Aida in the same area. The two magnets attract through the fabric and hold the front magnet in place. The grip should be firm; the front magnet should not slide or fall off easily.

When you want to rest the needle, lay it on the face of the Aida beside the front magnet. The front magnet pulls the needle toward it and holds it flat on the fabric surface. The needle is secure and immediately to hand.

To move the needle minder to a different position, slide the front magnet across the fabric while maintaining contact with the back magnet. The back magnet follows on the other side. There is no need to remove the back magnet and reinsert it.

items.symptom: The front magnet falls off the fabric
items.cause: The magnet pair is too weak for the Aida fabric weight, or the magnets are misaligned.
items.fix: Check that the back magnet is directly beneath the front magnet. If alignment is correct but the grip is weak, the magnet strength is insufficient for this fabric weight. Use a neodymium magnet pair rather than a ferrite pair for thicker fabric counts.

items.symptom: The needle minder is leaving a slight mark on the Aida surface
items.cause: The front magnet has a rough or uncoated back surface pressing against the fabric.
items.fix: Apply a small circle of felt or suede to the back surface of the front magnet. This cushions the contact with the Aida and prevents surface marking. Most commercial needle minders have a smooth back; if yours does not, check for sharp edges and file or cover them.

content.text: A needle minder is useful for any stitcher who works with multiple needles (one per colour), as each needle can be held on the fabric in its own position. Label the edge of the fabric near each needle with the thread colour number using a light pencil mark, so it is easy to return the right needle to the right colour when resuming.
